extracted.intended_audience: current or prospective mathematics department chairs and academic administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for chairs of mathematics departments on recruiting majors, managing curriculum, staff, faculty, and resources, and interacting with administration and donors. Focuses on concrete actions and standards a chair should follow to run an effective department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attracting and increasing undergraduate majors
rubrics_metrics.description: Design and implement initiatives to increase the number of math majors (e.g., new majors such as Computational Math, customizable 'roll your own' majors, strong minors, targeted promotion in large service classes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use creative programs (new majors/tracks, flexible majors, vigorous minor programs), improve counseling, have faculty pitch courses, invite good students to events, send emails to prospective majors. The Chair is responsible for tending the 'vineyard' and making things happen, with the Undergraduate Vice-Chair assisting but the Chair 'calling the shots'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undergraduate Vice-Chair responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Undergraduate Vice-Chair directs the undergraduate program: looks after majors, recruits more majors, manages graduation processes, selects students for awards, and attends ceremonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also oversees the undergraduate curriculum (contemporary/competitive comparisons with other departments), miscellaneous tasks (Putnam team, honors advising, undergrad lounge), delegates where appropriate, chairs an advisory committee, ensures course web pages and posted syllabi, posts faculty office hours, and may field student complaints or oversee advising depending on department structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic curriculum review and modernization
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly review and rethink the undergraduate (and graduate) mathematics curriculum to ensure it is contemporary, competitive, and fits current educational and workforce needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how the curriculum stacks up against related fields (Physics, Engineering, CS); consider roles of discrete math, algebra, cryptography, statistics, applied math; form a Taskforce via the Undergraduate Vice-Chair to study and recommend changes; enable cross-department collaboration so students can include non-math coursework and multiple thesis advisors when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff relations and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat departmental staff (secretaries, computer support, curriculum administrators) with respect, appreciation, and support; avoid tolerating faculty mistreatment of staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be friendly, show appreciation (lunches, small gifts), ask staff advice and listen, avoid micromanagement, let them do their jobs, and publicly defend and stand up for them when needed. A congenial, reliable staff simplifies the Chair's life; poor relations make it difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring, onboarding, and terminating staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Oversee hiring: interview candidates, assess technical proficiencies and people skills, check employment history and references; help train and acclimate new staff; make termination decisions when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: University typically screens applicants and administers tests, but Chair interviews and chooses (often with Office Manager). Ask relevant interview questions about technical skills, flexibility, hours, and reasons for job changes. Consult administrative offices and use available institutional processes for background checks and sensitive termination actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fostering faculty teamwork
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote and identify subsets of faculty who can function as team players to undertake large, coordinated departmental projects (e.g., curricular redesign, internships, major grant-driven research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that administrators value departments that can organize around big projects; recruit or highlight credible team members who are also good researchers and teachers to give the team credibility and help curry favor with Deans/Provosts. Understand cultural differences where mathematicians value individuality; work to find or build collaborators nonetheless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting faculty teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively support and reward effective teaching, and provide material and logistical support for classroom instruction and course development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reward excellent teachers at raise time with concrete information to present to the Dean. Provide equipment (projectors, computers, SmartBoards), ensure classrooms and lounges have suitable tech, fund extra grading time or TAs where warranted, support field trips, back new course proposals and curriculum changes by routing through appropriate review (Vice-Chair for Undergraduate Studies and committees). Use discretionary funds creatively to assist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting faculty research
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify, recognize, nurture, and resource faculty research efforts through travel funds, visitor support, equipment, and grant proposal assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide ample travel support (match needs to situation), consider reserve funds for visitor semesters, approve relatively inexpensive items readily (printers), weigh larger expenditures (RAID units, scanners) possibly via Executive Committee or shared equipment for multiple faculty, and help novice faculty with grant preparation or connect them to experienced mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing and managing endowed lecture series
rubrics_metrics.description: Create and maintain endowed lecture series to bring distinguished speakers, provide departmental cohesion, and build donor relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endowed series (modest endowment ~$40,000) are perennial events that provide honoraria and perks to attract speakers; use these events to involve donors, recognize them publicly, and cultivate larger gifts (potentially endowing Chairs). If none exist, spearhead fundraising with the Executive Committee and Development Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing faculty complaints and conflict resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Receive and manage faculty complaints constructively, using them as opportunities to exchange views and strengthen relations, while consulting appropriate institutional resources for serious matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop skills to deflect blame productively and catalyze cooperation. For serious allegations (sexual harassment, plagiarism, legal issues) consult legal/psychological specialists in administration before commenting. Use complaint handling to build trust and present yourself as steward of faculty interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty discipline and addressing dereliction
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle disciplinary matters—document misconduct (e.g., missed classes), follow institutional procedures, and engage the Dean/administration as needed for sanctions or termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For legal/serious misconduct (harassment, financial fraud) higher authorities will take over; in cases of teaching dereliction collect dates/times/consequences, attempt remediation, and if necessary coordinate threats or sanctions with the Dean, who has enforcement power. Early detection and intervention are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing high-profile ('prima donna') faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance the needs and demands of distinguished, high-profile faculty (salary, office, secretarial/time, travel funds) with fairness to other faculty and departmental budget constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the value they add to departmental prestige but avoid overallocating limited resources; negotiate with the Dean (e.g., secure an endowed Chair to shift costs off departmental budget) and make equitable decisions to retain overall morale and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to outside offers and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle faculty reports of outside job offers: gather full details, consider counter-offers (salary, load reductions, travel funds), and coordinate with the Dean to attempt retention when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess why the faculty member is considering leaving (institutional prestige, personal reasons, spouse/kids), collect specifics of the offer, and determine what the department/Dean can realistically do. Minor countermeasures (discretionary funds, reduced teaching load) may suffice; sometimes counter-offers are impossible or futile if the move is for a 'dream institution' or personal reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensuring adequate library and research access
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and advocate for a robust mathematics library collection (departmental library or strong presence in main library) and timely access to books and journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematicians need current books and journals at their fingertips; interlibrary loan is acceptable but can cause delays that hinder research. Strive for convenient access (departmental collection or efficient main library support) and a dedicated librarian if possible.
